paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: So when Ari came back to offer the water, I was like, oh, geez, change that story immediately. And so I made a big deal about rejoicing and tartuking about it. For another 500 pesos. This is for the more advanced students who know more. What did I just do? I did something else. And we'll leave it there for tonight.
{Audience sharing their answers}

paragraphs.speaker: Audience
paragraphs.text: You're changing your identity.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: That's true, but that's not the answer.

paragraphs.speaker: Audience
paragraphs.text: Because what you saw someone else do.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: That's true, but that's not the answer.
{inaudible answer}

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Okay, that’s not the answer but that worth another 500 pesos. So, for the people online: if you didn’t hear it, she said I was rejoicing in it to help all of you rejoice in it—so you plant the seed, which mean we’re planting seeds in a co-creating kind of way. So those seeds are multiplying even faster. But the answer I’m looking for is one word.

paragraphs.speaker: Audience
paragraphs.text: Angel Tartuk.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Oh… That’s… I run out of money. That is kind of the answer, but it’s not where I’m going. One word.

paragraphs.speaker: Audience
paragraphs.text: Change.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: No. We’ll save it for tomorrow night. It was up two. It was indirect. I didn't change the reality. Nope. Right. She got it. The word is four powers.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Because I planted a bad seed, a seed that I don't want, I immediately did a purification. And how did I do the purification? I did the whole thing in my head. There are four steps to purify.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: What's the first step of purifying a seed? Let’s say remember the pen. In the sense that it's the idea that things are coming from seeds. The first step is recognizing: well, I planted a seed, but I also didn't have control of when I planted it, because it just happened — which came from the past. What's the second step?

paragraphs.speaker: Audience
paragraphs.text: The intelligent regret.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Right. You feel… You recognize that that seed is going to have to ripen. The first step is recognizing, “Well, I planted the seed, but I also didn’t controlled of what I planted because it just happened which came from the past.” Then you think, “Well, that seed's going to go into the future and grow; who’s going to come out? ‘Boring Tim’—a Tim who thinks they’re boring.” What's the third step? Stop doing it again. I'm not going to do that again. Then the fourth step: you do some kind of makeup activity.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Now, am I always going to be able to stop the boring seeds — the Tim that thinks he's boring from the past? Am I going to be able to stop all of them? No. But I make the wish that it can end. And the fact that when it happened, I didn't engage it for too long. It's like, wow, I wonder if I bored her. I don't want to be that person. And I just stopped it.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: This is the reason I don't want to teach in Spanish. Because I can't have half my brain doing that and half my brain doing this. Eventually I'll be able to speak as well in Spanish — this is my goal. But notice that limiting thing came out from my mouth without even thinking about it. I even did it in the form of a joke, “Hey, look—this is why I’m not speaking Spanish. Because I cannot do this. I can’t teach in Spanish because I can’t use the other part of my brain.” Yes, It's difficult when you're speaking not your language. But I just made it impossible, by using the words… and not event the words but I got it. I was it. Not even I thought, but I was that person.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Entonces voy a dar la última parte de clase en español para que no... blah, blah, blah, blah, blah.

paragraphs.speaker: Interpreter
paragraphs.text: So I'm going to teach you the last part of the class in Spanish so that... blah, blah, blah, blah, blah.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: And then I gave up. But did you see how I did the purification, the four powers, immediately? I am tartuk-ing in the beautiful kindness that I saw. I am that. I am that. The seed opened as me and that. And I want that. I want more of it. And I got you to rejoice in it, so then your seed will grow. So now we have lots more of it.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: All right. So tomorrow we will continue. And tomorrow we're going to do more of a workshop kind of class, where we're going to dive in and do some work of — what are some of these limiting beliefs that you may have, so you can shine some light onto it? And then from there, we're going to turn that into a discussion on leadership.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: And if you never come back, I'll tell you the secret right now.
{audience laughs} Buenas noches. No, no, no. It’s so awesome.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: When you release those limiting beliefs and truly change that, and change who you are — leadership is automatic. You don't have to do anything else.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Change you, and then your world changes. And the point of automatic leadership is not so you can be el jefe o la jefa (boss). That's not the point of leadership. The point of it is much deeper. How do you raise other people, uplift other people? Because leaders come and go. Lives come and go.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: But what was that impact that you can tartuk in that last moment of your life?

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: And tomorrow we'll talk a little bit more about it.

paragraphs.speaker: Host (Aldo Arzapalo)
paragraphs.text: Muchas gracias a todos. Thank you for joining. Thank you, everyone here and online. Thank you, team, for this.
